questions.question: Which hyperscaler strategy is best described as a model marketplace — offering Claude, Llama, Titan, Cohere, and Stability behind a single API?
options: Azure OpenAI
AWS Bedrock
Vertex AI
Fireworks AI
questions.explanation: AWS Bedrock is the marketplace: multiple third-party and first-party models behind one API and one IAM surface. Azure OpenAI is an exclusive OpenAI partnership; Vertex AI is Gemini-first.

questions.question: What are Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) in Azure OpenAI?
options: Per-token credits that roll over monthly
Reserved blocks of inference GPU capacity priced per hour
Shared on-demand GPU pools shared across all tenants
Rate-limit tokens that throttle requests above a threshold
questions.explanation: PTUs reserve dedicated GPU capacity for your tenant, eliminating contention with other customers. That is why Azure OpenAI can achieve ~50 ms median TTFT versus Bedrock on-demand's ~75 ms on equivalent models.

questions.question: Artificial Analysis benchmarks show Azure OpenAI at ~50 ms median TTFT on Llama 3.1 405B-class deployments versus Bedrock at ~75 ms. What best explains this gap?
options: Azure uses newer H200 GPUs while Bedrock still runs H100s
Azure PTUs provide dedicated capacity while Bedrock defaults to shared on-demand
Bedrock routes through an additional IAM layer adding latency
Azure compresses responses at the edge before delivery
questions.explanation: PTUs reserve capacity — your tenant is not competing with others. Bedrock's on-demand model uses shared capacity, so latency varies with overall cluster load. The gap is a capacity-model difference, not a hardware difference.

questions.question: Which FinOps attribution mechanism is described as the cleanest native solution for per-feature cost breakdown in 2026?
options: Vertex AI project-per-team with BigQuery billing export
Azure resource-group tags with Application Insights
Bedrock Application Inference Profiles with CloudWatch
OpenAI organization usage dashboard with per-key reporting
questions.explanation: Bedrock Application Inference Profiles (added 2025) let you tag a profile with team/product/feature and route all invocations through it; CloudWatch breaks out cost per profile without post-processing. It is described as the most granular hyperscaler-native attribution.

questions.question: What is the recommended policy to mitigate single-hyperscaler lock-in for product-critical LLM calls in 2026?
options: One-provider minimum with a quarterly review of alternatives
Two-provider minimum with failover between them via a gateway
Three-provider minimum — one per hyperscaler — with round-robin routing
Use only the Anthropic direct API to avoid lock-in to any hyperscaler
questions.explanation: The lesson prescribes a two-provider minimum — commonly Bedrock plus Azure OpenAI — with a gateway routing optimally between them. Single-hyperscaler commitment is the expensive mistake because the frontier model changes quarterly across providers.

questions.question: At approximately what sustained utilization does an Azure PTU reservation break even versus on-demand pricing?
questions.explanation: The lesson states PTU break-even is usually around 40-60% sustained utilization. Below that, on-demand is cheaper because you avoid paying for idle reserved capacity. At high utilization PTUs offer up to 70% savings.
